Cheng: Bringing up hf-ft-quantized checkpoint (meta/llama-13b-quant8) — tool-calling tests failing: JSON-mode outputs are getting mangled after quantization. Anyone seen special-token splits after fast-tokenizer merges?
Maria: Yep, saw this on the nightly eval — tool-call success rate dropped ~18% vs fp16 baseline. Looks like the JSON-mode sentinel gets split across BPE boundaries.
Sam: Can you paste a quick repro?
Cheng: Sure — minimal repro:
```
# prompt snippet
prompt = 'Assistant: please call the tool with 
<json>{"action":"search","q":"llm serving"}</json>'
# tokenized (fast tokenizer, after quantize):
['Assistant', ':', 'please', 'call', 'the', 'tool', 'with', '<', 'json', '>', '{', '\"action', '\":', '\"search', '\",', '\"q\"', ':', '\"llm', 'serving', '\"', '}', '<', '/', 'json', '>']
```
Cheng: Note how '< json >' is split into three tokens. Our JSON-mode parser expects a single sentinel token; split tokens break the JSON extractor and the tool-call schema.
Lee: That matches my local bisect — the fast tokenizer merges were regenerated during the quant pipeline and we didn't re-register the special tokens. The correct approach is to add the entire sentinel as a single special token via tokenizer.add_special_tokens({ 'additional_special_tokens': ['<json>','</json>','<tool>','</tool>'] }) and re-export the tokenizer files.
Maria: We tried putting them in config.json under 'special_tokens', but the runtime mapping layer expects the tokenizer to emit a single token id; a config string alone didn't prevent the BPE from splitting on some merges.
ci-bot: nightly/toolcall-eval failed 2026-01-12 04:12 UTC — regressions: tool-call success -18%, hallucination up slightly. See CI run: https://ci/internal/12345
Sam: Short-term mitigation: we can add a lightweight post-tokenize pass in the serving runtime that merges sequences ['<','json','>'] -> '<json>' before feeding into the parser. That avoids blocking a canary. Example:
```python
def merge_json_tokens(tokens):
    out=[]
    i=0
    while i < len(tokens):
        if i+2 < len(tokens) and tokens[i]=='<' and tokens[i+1]=='json' and tokens[i+2]=='>' :
            out.append('<json>')
            i += 3
        else:
            out.append(tokens[i])
            i += 1
    return out
```
Lee: That would be fine as a stopgap, but long-term we must re-run tokenizer export with the special tokens baked in so all downstream infra (token ids, KV cache mapping, quant tables) are consistent. I'll prepare a tokenizer-export PR that: 1) adds tokens, 2) pins merges for the release, 3) bumps tokenizer.json in model artifact.
Maria: I'll re-run our tool-call eval harness against the new tokenizer + quant config once Lee lands. Also we should include a regression test where the prompt includes nested role tokens + tool tags — that's where we saw the worst failures.
Cheng: Plan/owners: Lee = tokenizer export PR (blocker for long-term), Sam = runtime post-tokenize merge (canary patch), Maria = eval reruns and regression tests, Cheng = docs + rollout notes + update model bring-up checklist. Can we target canary by EOD tomorrow?
Sam: I can get the runtime patch in a branch today, run quick canary by morning.
Lee: Starting tokenizer PR now. Will tag @Maria when ready.
Maria: Thx — I'll queue evals.
Cheng: Awesome. Adding checklist item: verify special tokens survive quant merge and appear as single token ids in tokenizer.json. :thumbsup:
Sam: :thumbsup:
